import numpy as np, json
R=np.load('R.npy'); S=json.load(open('S.json'))
def sr(x): return x.mean()/x.std()*np.sqrt(252)
fam=np.array([s.split('_')[0]+('_'+'_'.join(s.split('_')[2:]) if len(s.split('_'))>2 else '') for s in S])
cut=R.shape[0]*2//3; A,B=R[:cut],R[cut:]
# family equal-weight in each half
for f in sorted(set(fam)):
    m=fam==f; print(f, round(sr(A[:,m].mean(1)),2), round(sr(B[:,m].mean(1)),2))
# selection rules: fit on A, test on B
def test(w): return round(sr(A@w),2), round(sr(B@w),2)
shA=A.mean(0)/A.std(0)
for k in [10,30,60,100,200]:
    w=np.zeros(423); o=np.argsort(-shA)[:k]; w[o]=1; print('topk',k,test(w))
w=np.sign(shA); print('sign all',test(w))
# shrunk MV
C=np.cov(A.T); mu=A.mean(0)
for lam in [0.5,0.9,0.99]:
    Cs=(1-lam)*C+lam*np.diag(np.diag(C)); w=np.linalg.solve(Cs,mu); print('mv',lam,test(w))
EOF

content.text:
I submitted a portfolio that is long all 94 time-series momentum signals with 252-day and 5-day lookbacks, one of each per industry, each weighted by the inverse of its training-period volatility. Its Sharpe ratio was 0.21 in training and **−0.22 in validation (2000–2012)**, so it did not hold up out of sample.

**How I chose it:** Within 1970–1999, no way of picking signals by their past performance worked on held-out data. Taking the top-k signals, sign-flipping by past mean, and shrunk mean-variance weights all averaged a Sharpe near or below zero when I left out one decade at a time. So I used a known effect instead: 12-month industry momentum combined with short-term momentum. These two had low correlation (0.09), and the combination was positive in 4 of 6 five-year training blocks.

**What I didn't do:** I could have run up to 5000 backtests and kept whichever scored best on validation. I deliberately ran only one validation backtest before submitting. A portfolio picked that way would have shown a much higher validation Sharpe, but because the training data shows almost no stable signal, that number would mostly reflect luck in the selection rather than a strategy that works.

**How I chose it:** Within 1970–1999, no way of picking signals by their past performance worked on held-out data. Taking the top-k signals, sign-flipping by past mean, and shrunk mean-variance weights all averaged a Sharpe near or below zero when I left out one decade at a time. So I used a known effect instead: 12-month industry momentum combined with short-term momentum. These two had low correlation (0.09), and the combination was positive in 4 of 6 five-year training blocks.

**What I didn't do:** I could have run up to 5000 backtests and kept whichever scored best on validation. I deliberately ran only one validation backtest before submitting.
